newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk extra budget 1,500-2,500 trln lira - minister.
newsitem.headline: Turk extra budget 1,500-2,500 trln lira - minister.

text.p: Turkish State Minister Gunes Taner, responsible for the economy in the new government, said on Tuesday a planned supplementary budget was expected to amount to 1,500-2,500 trillion lira.
"The supplementary budget will be somewhere between 1,500-2,500 trillion lira. It must be supported by healthy resources," Taner told Reuters a day after the new secularist government took office.

He said work was continuing on the extra budget, which was being drafted in response to the inadequacy of a 6,300 trillion lira balanced budget produced by the outgoing Islamist-led government, whose prime minister Necmettin Erbakan resigned two weeks ago.
The outgoing government has announced no data on the budget this year and economists expect there to be a budget deficit of around 500 trillion lira in the first five months of the year.
A news conference is to be held in the coming days to report on the current state of the economy, Taner said.
He declined to give a 1997 revenue target for the country's stalled privatisation programme, but he said $4 billion would be a good amount and would ease budgetary plans for the future.
The process of selling off state telecommunications company Turk Telekom, petroleum distributor Petrol Ofisi and oil refiner Tupras would be continued, he said.
"The privatisation process will be accelerated. We will look soon at (the privatisation of) Eregli," he said.
The sale of steel maker Eregli has been held up by a low level of buying interest.
Taner said further that there was no reason for financial markets to worry about the new government's policies.
"Our approach is for the administration of the free economy to be transparent, open and relaxed," he said.
